title: [Shortcut Guide] Default "Hold Windows key" behavior interferes with Win+V and Win+H

actions.label: Explain Windows-key-hold scope limitation
actions.note: Draft a maintainer scope comment for the Windows-key-hold limitation.

comment.body: I re-checked the current Shortcut Guide activation flow, and this looks like a limitation of the **Hold Windows key** feature rather than a narrow module bug. When that hold timer expires, Shortcut Guide intentionally surfaces a foreground overlay. Windows surfaces such as Clipboard History, Voice Typing, and the new Find My Mouse Pointer also rely on Windows-key-hold behavior, so they can be dismissed once the Shortcut Guide overlay takes focus and then closes. I would answer this as product-scope feedback on the bare-Windows-key trigger model, not as a small corrective bug fix.

issue_context.summary: Shortcut Guide’s optional “Hold Windows key” activation conflicts with Windows hold-based shells because the overlay is intentionally foregrounded after the hold threshold expires.
known_information: The report covers Win+V, Win+H, and a follow-up comment adds Windows 11 Find My Mouse Pointer.
The issue is already marked Status-Reproducible and assigned.
ShortcutGuideModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp requests special runner handling for a held Windows key.
ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/OverlayWindow.xaml.cs explicitly brings the overlay to the foreground and activates it.
The centralized runner hook only tracks a held Windows key; it does not turn these OS gestures into separate module-specific signals after the hold overlay has already appeared.
inferences: Once Shortcut Guide wins the foreground after a Windows-key hold, Windows shell surfaces that expect to remain active across modifier release can be dismissed when that overlay closes.

The clean fix is not a small bug patch inside Clipboard History or Voice Typing interaction; it is a higher-level decision about whether bare Windows-key hold should remain a Shortcut Guide trigger at all.
issue_context.analysis: This is not well-scoped bug-fix work for the dashboard. The current source and comments both point to a limitation of the activation model rather than to a narrowly isolated code defect.
initial_investigation: Confirmed the overlay is intentionally signaled from a dedicated Windows-key hold event and then moved to the foreground.
Re-read the maintainer comment explaining why Windows shell surfaces close when the Shortcut Guide overlay closes.

judgment.rationale: Current Shortcut Guide behavior is tied to the product choice of stealing a bare Windows-key hold and surfacing a foreground overlay; that overlay necessarily conflicts with other Windows hold gestures once it takes focus.
evidence: ShortcutGuideActivationPolicy only shows the overlay for `WindowsKeyHold` when the configured Windows-key action is enabled.
ShortcutGuideModuleInterface/dllmain.cpp asks the centralized runner hook to track the pressed Windows key and signal a dedicated hold event after the configured timeout.
OverlayWindow.xaml.cs explicitly brings the overlay to the foreground and activates it.
A maintainer already noted in the issue that Clipboard History and Voice Typing close when the foreground window (Shortcut Guide) closes.
The second commenter confirms the same conflict pattern with Windows 11 Find My Mouse Pointer, another Windows-key hold surface.
judgment.recommended_action: Treat this as a product-scope limitation of the Windows-key-hold activation model and respond with that scope note instead of filing a narrow bug-fix design.

fix_assessment.rationale: Within the current design, Shortcut Guide intentionally owns a bare Win-key hold and foregrounds an overlay; avoiding every OS hold-gesture conflict would require a product-level trigger-model change rather than a small bug fix.
